claims.claim: Classic: raw Py4JJavaError for RDD Python failures with 'Caused by: org.apache.spark.api.python.PythonException' holding the Python traceback; eager analysis at select. Connect: analysis deferred to action or schema access; errors in pyspark.errors.exceptions.connect subclass SparkConnectGrpcException and are caught by pyspark.errors.AnalysisException; message includes 'JVM stacktrace:'; spark.sparkContext raises JVM_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_SUPPORTED.
claims.source: Local runs on PySpark 4.0.4, classic local[1] and remote('local[1]'), September 2026.

claims.claim: Serverless compute supports only Spark Connect APIs, not RDD APIs, and defers analysis and name resolution to execution time.

concept_html:
PySpark talks to the Spark engine in one of two ways, and each shapes the errors you see. Facts below were checked on PySpark 4.0.4 and the Databricks docs in September 2026.

Spark Classic runs your Python next to a JVM driver through Py4J. PySpark converts most engine errors into Python classes such as AnalysisException. Some still arrive raw, as py4j.protocol.Py4JJavaError:

Py4JJavaError: An error occurred while calling
z:org.apache.spark.api.python.PythonRDD.collectAndServe.
: org.apache.spark.SparkException: Job aborted due to stage failure ...
Caused by: org.apache.spark.api.python.PythonException: Traceback ...
  File "/repo/job.py", line 5, in <lambda>
ZeroDivisionError: division by zero

Skip the Java frames. Search for the last Caused by: line and the Python traceback inside it. That is your bug.

Spark Connect sends a query plan to a remote server over gRPC. Databricks serverless compute uses Spark Connect, and supports only Spark Connect APIs. Three differences matter when you debug:

  • Analysis is deferred. Classic Spark rejects a misspelt column when you call select. Spark Connect accepts the select and raises AnalysisException at the action, or when you read df.columns or df.schema. A try around the select catches nothing.
  • Error classes live in pyspark.errors.exceptions.connect. They subclass SparkConnectGrpcException and the familiar base classes, so except pyspark.errors.AnalysisException still works. The message ends with a JVM stacktrace: section from the server.
  • JVM-only attributes fail. spark.sparkContext raises [JVM_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_SUPPORTED]. RDD code, such as sc.parallelize, does not run on serverless.

Two habits follow. Catch pyspark.errors classes, never Py4JJavaError, so the same code works on both. And place error handling around the action, where both modes raise, not around the transformation.

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
columns = [c for c in (key_column, optional_column) if c in df.columns]
selected = df.select(*[F.col(c) for c in columns])
try:
selected.write.mode("append").saveAsTable(target_table)
except AnalysisException as err:
raise RuntimeError(f"write to {target_table} failed: {err.getCondition()}") from err

exercises.prompt: Write `python_cause(message: str) -> str | None`. Given the text of a Py4J error, return the last line of the Python traceback in the **last** `Caused by: org.apache.spark.api.python.PythonException` section: the first non-blank line that does not start with whitespace, `Traceback` or `File`, after that marker. Return `None` if there is no such section.
exercises.prompt_html: Write python_cause(message: str) -> str | None. Given the text of a Py4J error, return the last line of the Python traceback in the last Caused by: org.apache.spark.api.python.PythonException section: the first non-blank line that does not start with whitespace, Traceback or File, after that marker. Return None if there is no such section.
exercises.solution:
MARKER = "Caused by: org.apache.spark.api.python.PythonException:"


def python_cause(message: str) -> str | None:
    """Python exception line inside the last PythonException of a Py4J error.

    Args:
        message: Full error text.

    Returns:
        The exception line, such as "ZeroDivisionError: division by zero", or None.
    """
    if MARKER not in message:
        return None
    section = message.rsplit(MARKER, 1)[1]
    for line in section.splitlines()[1:]:
        if not line.strip() or line[0].isspace():
            continue
        if line.startswith(("Traceback", "File")):
            continue
        return line
    return None

title: Py4J and Spark Connect errors
why_html: A notebook wrapped df.select(col(name)) in try/except AnalysisException to skip columns missing from older waves. It worked on a classic cluster. After the team moved the job to serverless, the except never fired: the select succeeded, and the write failed with the same AnalysisException two cells later. Checking name in df.columns before the select works in both modes.
